title: ContraDB's ¶
assumes: Three places, taken one at a time, exactly where ContraDB's pilcrows are: the robins' pull-by right, number two's pull-by left, and the star through with number four.
quotes: ContraDB: “6: ladles balance & pull by right to 2nd 1st neighbors ⁋ · 2: 2nd neighbors pull by left ⁋ … 4: 4th 1st neighbors star through ⁋”
notes: ContraDB marks the figure that carries the progression with a pilcrow, and this dance has three of them. So the triple progression is `{ lark: 1, robin: 1 }` claimed by three calls rather than one claim of three, and the relations move with it: ContraDB (like the Caller's Box) numbers the neighbours from the top of the time through, while a record reads them from the seating the call is danced in — so the card's N2 at the second pull-by is written N1, its N3 at the square through is N1, its N4 at the twirl is N2, and its N4 at B2's ring is N1. **Measured** at six couples: `closure 39.1973 · progressed 68.0000 · reach 18.1906 short · collision 0.000`, against the record's `0.0000 · 20.0000 · 14.3567 · 0.246`, and the same at every length from five up. Writing the relations the reading's own way is the better of the two encodings and that was measured: left as the card writes them — N2, N3, N4 counted from the top of the time through — reach is 18.19–49.92 px short instead of 18.19–26.81.
